_readme: Shared image catalog for both the Notes viewer and the Hardware Identification game. 'file' is relative to assets/images/<category>/ -- never write a full path. Set 'quiz' to null for reference diagrams that should be readable in notes but never appear as a guessing-game prompt. See assets/notes/_TEMPLATE.md for how notes reference these images.

quiz.explanation: The 24-pin ATX connector (also called 20+4) is the primary power connector for modern motherboards, providing +12V, +5V, +3.3V, and ground to the system.
RG-6 is commonly used for cable television, satellite, and broadband internet. It has better shielding than RG-59 and lower attenuation over longer distances.
DisplayPort supports higher resolutions and refresh rates than HDMI, with bandwidth up to 32.4 Gbps. It uses a distinctive latch connector.

options: D-Sub DB-15 VGA analog video standard
quiz.explanation: DVI-D carries digital-only video signals. The dual-link variant can support higher resolutions. DVI-I combines both analog and digital on one connector.
The 8-pin EPS connector (or 4+4 pin) provides +12V power exclusively to the CPU, ensuring stable overclocking headroom. It can supply up to 150W.
This patch cable uses multi-mode fiber (OM3/OM4) with LC (small form factor) on one end and SC (snap/slide) on the other for data center interconnects.
HDMI 2.1 is the newest standard with significantly higher bandwidth, supporting 8K resolution and 120 Hz refresh rates with enhanced color depth.
The Molex connector is a classic 4-pin power connector used in older systems. It provides +12V and +5V to legacy devices. Many newer adapters convert to SATA.
The 6+2 pin PCIe connector can be configured as either 6-pin (75W) or 8-pin (150W) depending on modular cable routing. High-end cards may need dual 8-pin connections.
RJ-11 is the standard 6-position modular connector for analog telephone lines. It's physically similar to but smaller than RJ-45, with only 2-4 active contacts.
Standard RJ-45 cables are typically Cat 5e or Cat 6. Cat 6 supports gigabit speeds reliably up to 100 meters with better shielding than Cat 5e.
SATA 3.0 (6 Gbps) is the current standard for connecting SSDs and mechanical drives. It replaced IDE/PATA with hot-swappable L-shaped connectors.
USB 3.0 (SuperSpeed) uses Type-A connectors with distinctive blue inserts internally. It's 5 Gbps, 10x faster than USB 2.0, and backward compatible.
Micro-USB is a 5-pin connector standard on Android phones and many IoT devices. Type-A to Micro-USB cables are universal charging bridges.
USB Type-B (square connector) is commonly used on printers, scanners, and older external drives. Type-A is the standard rectangular host connector.
USB-C is a 24-pin reversible connector supporting USB 3.1 (10 Gbps), Thunderbolt 3 (40 Gbps), and power delivery up to 240W depending on implementation.
VGA (Video Graphics Array) is a 15-pin D-Sub analog connector carrying red, green, blue, horizontal/vertical sync, and ground. It's largely obsolete but still found in some environments.
AIO coolers use a sealed liquid loop with a pump block, radiator, and fans. They offer superior cooling compared to air coolers and are popular for gaming/overclocking.
A PWM splitter allows connecting multiple 4-pin PWM fans to a single motherboard header. The motherboard controls all fans together with common PWM signal.
M.2 heatsinks are passive aluminum spreaders that dissipate NVMe heat through conduction. They prevent thermal throttling during sustained I/O load.
Tower coolers are tall air-cooled heatsinks with aluminum fins and copper heatpipes. They offer excellent cooling performance comparable to AIO at lower cost and noise.
VRM (Voltage Regulator Module) heatsinks dissipate heat from MOSFETs and inductors. Better heatsinks improve stability and longevity during overclocking.
Delidding exposes the bare silicon die by removing the IHS (Integrated Heat Spreader). Enthusiasts delid for better cooling contact, but voids warranty and risks damage.
The IHS is the metal cap (usually copper/nickel) soldered to the CPU die. It protects the silicon and provides a surface for cooler contact and thermal transfer.
LGA 1700 (Land Grid Array with 1700 pins) is Intel's socket for 12th and 13th gen Core processors (Alder Lake, Raptor Lake). Pins are on the motherboard, not CPU.
LGA processors have flat contact pads on the bottom. The motherboard socket has pins that make contact. LGA is more fragile than PGA but allows denser packaging.
PGA (Pin Grid Array) processors have pins on the bottom that insert into socket holes. Used by AMD (AM4/AM5) and older Intel. More robust than LGA during installation.
DDR3 uses a 240-pin DIMM form factor with 1.5V operating voltage. Common speeds range 1333-1866 MHz. Succeeded DDR2 and preceded DDR4.
DDR4 runs at 2133-4000+ MHz with a 288-pin DIMM. It has lower voltage (1.2V vs 1.5V for DDR3), but higher latency. Standard for desktop/server 2013-2021.
DDR5 operates at 4800+ MHz with 288 pins (same physical size as DDR4 but incompatible). Key feature: each DIMM has its own Power Delivery Module (PDM).
SO-DIMM (Small Outline DIMM) is compact memory for laptops. DDR3 SO-DIMM has 204 pins, while DDR4/DDR5 have 260 pins. Same speed grades as desktop equivalents.
2.5" SATA SSDs are common in laptops and budget builds. They connect via SATA (6 Gbps) and run much faster than mechanical drives but slower than NVMe.
Standard 3.5" HDDs spin at 7200 RPM with 64MB cache. Despite slower random access than SSDs, they offer high capacity at lowest cost for bulk storage.

options: microSD card for mobile and IoT devices
quiz.explanation: CompactFlash (CF) was popular in cameras and industrial equipment with ATA/IDE interface. Capacities reached 256GB. Now obsolete, replaced by SD family.
External HDDs pair a 3.5" or 2.5" drive with USB adapter for portable storage. They offer large capacity for backups. USB provides both data and power.
M.2 NVMe SSDs use PCIe lanes directly, bypassing SATA bottleneck. PCIe 4.0 reaches ~7 GB/s, 10x faster than SATA. Standard form factors: 2242, 2260, 2280.
M.2 SATA SSDs use the compact M.2 physical form but limit throughput to SATA's 6 Gbps. These are slower than NVMe but cheaper than true NVMe drives.
RAID arrays combine multiple drives: RAID 0 (striping/speed), RAID 1 (mirroring/redundancy), RAID 5/6 (striped parity). Used in servers and NAS.
The inverter converts DC to high-frequency AC (600-1000V) to power CCFL backlight lamps. Modern laptops use LED backlights with simpler drivers instead.

options: DisplayPort Mini DP on compact displays
quiz.explanation: DVI ports on monitors and GPUs carry digital (DVI-D) or mixed (DVI-I) signals. DVI-D has 24 pins, DVI-I has 27 with integrated analog support.
LVDS is a low-voltage differential standard for laptop displays. Modern laptops increasingly use eDP (embedded DisplayPort) or USB-C video instead.
LCD monitors use a TFT backlight (LED nowadays) behind liquid crystal cells. They replaced CRTs due to lower power, smaller size, and better image quality.
OLED pixels emit their own light, eliminating backlight. Benefits: perfect blacks, high contrast, thin profile. Drawbacks: burn-in risk, lower peak brightness than LCD.
Almost all modern touchscreens use capacitive sensing. They detect the electrical properties of a conductive (finger) touch. Resistive screens required pressure.
VGA (Video Graphics Array) is the classic 15-pin D-Sub analog port. Carries RGB + sync signals. Largely obsolete, replaced by DVI/HDMI/DisplayPort.
M.2 adapter cards add NVMe slots to systems with limited M.2 ports. They use PCIe x4 or x8 lanes and appear as additional NVMe devices.
Video capture cards digitize HDMI/SDI signals in real-time. Used for streaming, recording, and video production. Can support 4K depending on specs.
PCIe risers and adapters help fit graphics cards or other expansion cards in space-constrained builds like small form factor or mining rigs.
Sound cards provide superior audio with dedicated DAC and amplifiers. Mostly obsolete for consumer, but pro audio still uses dedicated interfaces.
WiFi cards add or upgrade wireless connectivity. Modern cards support WiFi 6 (802.11ax) with faster speeds. Some boards have built-in WiFi.
Discrete GPUs slot into PCIe x16 with full bandwidth. Modern high-end cards need dual 8-pin power connectors. Support PCIe 3.0/4.0/5.0 standards.
High-speed network cards (10 GbE, 25 GbE) use PCIe x16 for adequate bandwidth. Commonly found in servers and workstations, not consumer desktops.
PCI (not PCIe) is a legacy 32-bit bus running 33 MHz max: 133 MB/s. It's functionally obsolete but some older machines still have PCI slots.
RAID controllers have dedicated processors and cache RAM for RAID parity calculations. Improves performance vs. software RAID by offloading CPU.
Lithium-ion batteries dominate mobile/laptop due to high energy density (150+ Wh/kg) and lack of memory effect. Degradation occurs over time/heat cycles.
MicroSD (microSecure Digital) is tiny flash storage common in Android phones and IoT devices. Supports UHS speeds and capacities to 1TB.
SIM cards authenticate to cellular networks. Modern phones switch to eSIM (embedded). SIM sizes: Full â†’ Mini â†’ Micro â†’ Nano (current standard).
The SIM tray slides out with an ejection tool, holding nano-SIM and optionally microSD. Improves serviceability vs. soldered modules.
Modern smartphone SoCs integrate CPU, GPU, modem, memory controllers, and NPU on a single chip. Examples: Snapdragon, Apple A-series, Exynos.
Access points provide WiFi coverage without routing. Used in enterprise settings behind a switch. Consumer routers combine AP, switch, and firewall.
SFP (1 Gig) transceivers plug into switch ports, converting electrical to optical. SFP+ (10G) and QSFP (40G/100G) are higher-bandwidth variants.
Patch panels terminate wall runs and connect to switches via short patch cables. Enables organized, rearrangeable network cabling in data centers.
Power over Ethernet (PoE) injectors combine data and power on one cable per 802.3at/bt standards. Eliminates separate power runs to cameras/APs.
Keystone jacks insert into wall plates and patch panels. Cat6/Cat6a keystones support different wiring standards (T568A/T568B).
Home WiFi routers integrate NAT routing, DHCP, firewall, wireless AP, and Ethernet switch. Enterprise deployments separate these functions.
Switches are Layer 2 devices learning MAC addresses and forwarding frames efficiently. Managed switches offer VLAN, PoE, and monitoring. Unmanaged are plug-and-play.
The 24-pin ATX connector delivers +12V, +5V, +3.3V to the motherboard. Modular PSUs often split it 20+4 for adaptability to both old and new boards.
Typical ATX desktop PSUs range 450-850W with 80+ certification (Bronze/Gold/Platinum). They convert AC mains to 12V, 5V, 3.3V rails.
Laptop adapters output DC (typically 19-20V). Modern laptops increasingly use USB-C PD (up to 240W), replacing proprietary connectors.
Molex 4-pin delivers +12V (two pins) and +5V (two pins). Once common for HDDs and peripherals. Now mostly obsolete, replaced by SATA.
Car inverters convert DC battery to AC for running laptops/tools in vehicles. Home/grid inverters do the reverse (solar DC to AC grid).
SATA power is 15-pin with three +12V rails, three +5V rails, and three GND pins. It replaced Molex for modern SSDs and mechanical drives.
UPS systems provide backup power during outages and condition AC (remove spikes). Common on servers for graceful shutdown time.
ESD wrist straps dissipate static from your body through a 1MÎ© resistor to ground. Essential when handling sensitive components like RAM and CPUs.
POST cards plug into ISA/PCI slot and display 2-digit hex codes during boot. Helps diagnose hang issues without display output.
Cable testers verify Ethernet cables for breaks and wiring faults. Advanced models show wire pairings and pin assignments.
Crimpers press the metal contacts inside RJ-45 connectors. Proper technique requires correct wire order and full conductor seating.
Multimeters measure voltage, current, and resistance. Essential for diagnosing power supply issues or testing continuity on cables/components.
Quality thermal paste application requires even coverage without air pockets. Spreaders help avoid excessive paste that degrades over time.
Torx T5/T6 bits are standard for laptop and server chassis. The 6-point design reduces cam-out compared to Phillips head.
The drum is the core component where toner sticks via static charge. It rotates and transfers the image to paper via the transfer roller.
The fuser applies heat (200Â°C+) and pressure to permanently bond toner powder to paper. Common failure point requiring replacement.
Impact ribbons spool continuously, being struck by pins to transfer ink. Still used in industrial/POS systems for reliability and multi-part forms.
Inkjet printers spray microscopic droplets. Thermal heads use heat to create bubbles; piezo heads use crystals. Lower cost but slower and higher per-page cost.
Print head cartridges integrate ink supply, heating elements/crystals, and micro-nozzles (100+ per color). They're the most expensive consumable.
Laser printers use a laser beam to charge the drum electrostatically, then toner adheres and fuses. Fast (40+ ppm) and economical per-page.
Thermal printers use heating elements on special paper. No toner/ink means low cost per page. Used for receipts, shipping labels, ID cards.
Toner cartridges are complex assemblies: OPC drum, developer roller, blade cleaner, and waste toner storage. They last 1000-10000+ pages.
The transfer belt (or transfer roller) moves paper under the charged drum, attracting toner. It requires occasional cleaning or replacement.
